items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: on the record was myself, Jack DeJohnette, Stanley Clarke, Freddie Hubbard, and a lot of people

ctx.x: Can you remember the worst thing you ever did? Would you like to?

You know I don’t know if I can remember. Well I do remember one, and I could, yeah I do remember what I consider probably to be actually one of the worst projects I ever did, maybe the worst, and there were some great people on it, but, and I won’t tell you the name of the person whose record it was because I’ve never heard from him since. I think he just, I think this was his one chance at trying to make a record. I don’t know if he was a tax write-off or if somebody just really liked him and just wanted to give…

had a couple of people I’ve spoken to and said oh yeah, I heard that record, man what a terrible, what a rotten record that is, why did you do that? I only had one answer. I did it for money. Somebody offered me extremely good money to fly me out and do this project and I figured well all these great musicians, it’s got to be good. And it wasn’t, and in a situation like that it wasn’t just that he didn’t sound good, nobody really sounded good. Everything just kind of came down to this base level of just — I mean…
